newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Mobutu troops terrorise new Congo residents.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu troops terrorise new Congo residents.

text.p: Remnants of the defeated army of dictator Mobutu Sese Seko are terrorising the Democratic Republic of Congo's eastern Kasai province, local residents said on Sunday.
They said the notoriously indisciplined soldiers had wreaked havoc in the Sankuru region in Kasai and called on President Laurent Kabila's forces to mop up the last pockets of resistance there.

"We don't know where these soldiers came from, but they have done so much harm to the locals. They have caused so much damage at gun point," Henri Lokandja, a Sankuru student who recently arrived in Kinshasa, told Reuters.

Speaking on state radio, a Sankuru resident said, "The ex-FAZ (Zaire army) are terrorising everybody there. They are looting, stealing, raping women and killing. They have so far burned down 30 houses."
He said most of the 6,000 Sankuru inhabitants had fled into a nearby forest.

State television said on Saturday that a delegation of Sankuru residents held talks with Interior minister Mwenze Kongolo in Kinshasa about the lack of security . The minister had promised to address the problem.
It quoted the minister as saying that the Alliance forces did not control Sankuru, which contains many towns including Lodja, Lomela and Lubefu.

Kabila's Tutsi-dominated Alliance forces launched a rebellion in eastern Kivu last October. They marched across the vast Central African country with no strong resistance from veteran president Mobutu's ragtag army.
They triumphantly entered the capital Kinshasa in May, putting an end to Mobutu's 32-year dictatorship.
Kabila has proclaimed himself president with sweeping powers. He has pledged to turn former Zaire, renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo, into a prosperous and peaceful state.
But the crime rate is still high in the nation of over 40 million people. Killings are regularly reported around the country, blamed on members of the disbanded army.
Jean Kalamasa, who does business in the interior of the country, said his trucks would not leave the capital until peace was restored to the Sankuru region.
"They (soldiers) have to be stopped from misbehaving. The whole country has been liberated apart from that part of eastern Kasai," Kalamasa told Reuters.
Defeated soldiers have been told to go to a training centre in Kitona, 400 km (240 miles) south-west of Kinshasa, to be absorbed into the new goverenment army.
Many have refused, describing the order as humiliating.
